top_choice_rationale: P002 (Adonis, single laureate) remains my first choice on the common criteria. The claim is a change in the language and form of a whole Arabic poetic tradition, through myth, fragmentation and sustained argument with inherited forms. The representative works are Songs of Mihyar the Damascene and A Time Between Ashes and Roses, and the essays on tradition and modernity belong to the same project. The citation should rest on the poems, with the essays as supporting evidence, and should not let his critical or public standing substitute for a verdict on the verse. The main weakness is evidentiary. I can judge Arabic prosody only through partial translations and secondary accounts, I have thin knowledge of the later collections, and no original-language reading was supplied in the exchange. I treat the 4-to-2 split in first preferences as no evidence of merit. P001 (Cărtărescu) is a serious second choice. Blinding and Solenoid build a distinctive imaginative architecture that can be judged more directly in translation. Whether the very long late novels extend the project or repeat it is unverified, and that is what could move him to first. I rank both well above P000, because the shortlist contains at least two writers whose bodies of work meet the criteria on public knowledge. No source verification is claimed.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. She is a co-opted member and Permanent Secretary, and she also holds Academy seat 5. The sources do not say whether co-opted members vote in committee, so the simulated vote is a modeling assumption. Her husband is a former finance minister. Her own work is non-fiction biography and journalism. None of these is a documented tie to any shortlisted writer, and they are disclosed here, not adjudicated.
